root_cause.text: `mddev_suspend()` could kill `mddev->active_io` and wait for it to drain without first waking raid456 IO threads blocked in `raid5_make_request()` on `wait_for_reshape`, so a frozen reshape left those waiters stuck holding an active_io reference and caused suspend to deadlock.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a `prepare_suspend` call in `drivers/md/md.c` specifically when `reshape_interrupted(mddev)` is true, with the comment that “RAID456 IO can sleep in wait_for_reshape while still holding an active_io reference” and must be woken “so they can abort and drop the reference instead of deadlocking suspend”; the CVE description likewise says `mddev_suspend()` “kills active_io and waits for all in-flight IO to drain” while reshape is frozen, preventing the reference from ever being dropped.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix mddev_suspend() to wake interrupted RAID reshape waiters so suspend does not deadlock waiting for active I/O references to drain.
intent_record.what: In mddev_suspend(), after percpu_ref_kill(&mddev->active_io), the code now conditionally calls mddev->pers->prepare_suspend(mddev) when mddev->pers exists, prepare_suspend is available, and reshape_interrupted(mddev) is true. A new comment explains that RAID456 I/O can sleep in wait_for_reshape while still holding an active_io reference, and that the added call wakes those waiters so they can abort and drop the reference before suspend waits for active_io to reach zero.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this change proactively unblocks reshape-related waiters that might otherwise remain asleep while still holding an active I/O reference, preventing mddev_suspend() from hanging indefinitely waiting for active_io to drain. It allows suspend to complete when reshape has already been interrupted or frozen by forcing the reshape waiters to wake up and exit cleanly.

grouping_result.intent: Fix mddev_suspend() to wake interrupted RAID reshape waiters so suspend does not deadlock waiting for active I/O references to drain.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: mddev_suspend() was deadlocking because it waited for active I/O to drain without waking RAID5/6 reshape waiters blocked in raid5_make_request(). The fix explicitly wakes those waiters so the active_io references can drain.

candidates.rationale: This statement disables the active_io reference counting and then suspend waits for it to drain. In the vulnerable path, it was done without first waking RAID456 threads stuck in raid5_make_request() on wait_for_reshape, so the active_io reference could remain held indefinitely and deadlock suspend.

This is the suspend wait that blocks until active_io reaches zero. Because the reshape waiters were not woken before entering this wait, the suspend path could block forever waiting for a reference that could not drain.
This condition is the drain check for suspend. It becomes false indefinitely when RAID456 I/O threads remain stuck holding active_io during a frozen reshape, directly contributing to the deadlock.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement starts suspend by killing active_io references. In the vulnerable path, it occurred before waking RAID456 reshape waiters, so threads stuck in raid5_make_request() on wait_for_reshape could keep an active_io reference forever and suspend would deadlock waiting for drain.

This is the suspend wait that blocks until active_io drains. Without first waking the frozen reshape waiters, this wait could never complete because the blocked RAID456 I/O threads still held the active_io reference.
This is the drain condition checked by suspend. If reshape waiters are not awakened, active_io may remain non-zero indefinitely, causing suspend to wait forever and deadlock.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is specifically that suspend could kill `mddev->active_io` and wait for it to drain *without first waking* raid456 I/O threads blocked in `raid5_make_request()` on `wait_for_reshape`. In this snippet, the new helper `__mddev_suspend()` explicitly includes the fix: after `percpu_ref_kill(&mddev->active_io);` it waits for drain, and immediately before marking the array suspended it documents the deadlock avoidance: `/* For raid456, io might be waiting for reshape to make progress, allow new reshape to start while waiting for io to be done to prevent deadlock. */` followed by `WRITE_ONCE(mddev->suspended, mddev->suspended + 1);`. Also, `__mddev_resume()` wakes the relevant threads via `md_wakeup_thread(mddev->thread);` and `md_wakeup_thread(mddev->sync_thread);`. Therefore the old deadlocking suspend path is not present in this new helper, and the fix is already present in the shown code.
